London is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable central heating installation and repair services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of London and the surrounding Greater London region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional central heating services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across Greater London, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any central heating installation and repair requirement.

We cover all postcodes across London with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: How long does a central heating installation take?
faqs.a: A full central heating installation in a 3-bedroom semi-detached property typically takes 3-5 days. Larger properties or complex layouts take longer.

faqs.q: How many radiators do I need?
faqs.a: A qualified heating engineer calculates the heat loss for each room based on size, insulation, window area, and orientation, then sizes radiators accordingly. Undersized radiators are the most common reason homes never get warm enough.

faqs.q: What is a power flush and do I need one?
faqs.a: A power flush forces water and chemicals through your heating system at high velocity to remove sludge and corrosion debris. It's recommended before fitting a new boiler to an old system — debris from old pipes can damage a new boiler within months.

faqs.q: Should I add inhibitor to my heating system?
faqs.a: Yes — inhibitor prevents internal corrosion and sludge buildup, extending the life of your boiler and pump significantly. It should be added to all new installations and refreshed every 2-3 years.

localParagraph: London's central heating landscape reflects the remarkable diversity of its housing stock, where Victorian terraces in Islington sit alongside post-war council blocks in Tower Hamlets and modern new-builds throughout the Docklands regeneration zones. This mixture of property ages and construction types across England's capital means that heating systems vary enormously from street to street, with older homes in areas like Clapham or Hackney often running on ageing boilers connected to radiator networks that have been patched and extended over decades. Water hardness adds another layer of complexity across London, as the mixed water hardness found throughout Greater London — ranging from moderately hard in outer boroughs to significantly harder supplies in parts of the south and east — accelerates limescale buildup within boilers and pipework. This gradual scaling reduces system efficiency and shortens component lifespan considerably, making regular servicing and the installation of scale inhibitors particularly worthwhile investments for homeowners. Experienced heating engineers familiar with both the local water conditions and the varied building types across London can provide genuinely tailored maintenance and installation advice.
whatItInvolves: Central heating installation or replacement involves fitting a new boiler, radiators, pipework, and controls to heat your home efficiently. A full system installation is a major project typically taking 3-5 days. A system upgrade — replacing radiators and adding smart controls to an existing boiler — takes 1-2 days. Both must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer.
process: Survey: calculate heat loss per room and size radiators accordingly. First fix: run new pipework routes, fit radiator brackets, position boiler location. Second fix: hang radiators, connect boiler, fit programmer and thermostatic radiator valves. Commission: fill system, add inhibitor, balance radiators for even heat distribution, test all controls. Register with Building Control. Full system flush prior to filling removes debris that causes cold spots and pump failure.
whatToExpect: A full central heating installation in a 3-bed semi takes 3-5 days. You'll be without heating and hot water during the works — plan around this in winter. Modern systems with smart thermostats (Nest, Hive, Tado) can reduce heating bills by 20-30% through accurate scheduling. Your installer should provide a full commission certificate and Building Regulations notification.
